 India VIX Closes at 17.55, as US Inflation Concerns and Geopolitical Risks Offset Domestic Market Gains 
 India VIX Closes at 17.55, as US Inflation Concerns and Geopolitical Risks Offset Domestic Market Gains
 Authored By HDFC SKY | Published at: Nov 11, 2026 04:10 PM IST

 Mumbai, 11 November 2026: India VIX ended Wednesday’s trading session at 17.55, rising 0.13 points or 0.75% from its previous close of 17.42, as developments across domestic and global markets shaped volatility during the session. The index opened at 17.42, touched an intraday high of 17.82 and declined to a low of 15.64 before settling higher. The session saw a sharp opening rally in benchmark indices, followed by afternoon profit-booking, while concerns surrounding US inflation, Federal Reserve policy, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments remained relevant to market movements.
 India VIX Rises 0.75% To 17.55 After Touching 17.82 During The Session 
 India VIX, which measures the market’s expectation of near-term volatility based on Nifty 50 index options, closed at 17.55, compared with its previous closing level of 17.42. The index opened unchanged at 17.42 and recorded a trading range of 15.64–17.82 during Wednesday’s session. Its 52-week range stood between 8.72 and 28.90, while its year-to-date return was 85.13%.
 The movement came after India VIX declined 5.48% to 17.42 in the previous trading session on 9 November. Indian equity markets remained closed on 10 November on account of Diwali Balipratipada. The volatility index subsequently recorded a marginal increase on Wednesday, ending above its opening and previous closing levels.
 The index’s daily technical rating remained Neutral. Its pivot point stood at 17.54 under the Classic, Fibonacci and Camarilla methods. Under the Classic method, resistance levels were 18.32, 19.21 and 19.99, while support levels were 16.65, 15.87 and 14.98. The Fibonacci resistance levels were 18.18, 18.58 and 19.21, with supports at 16.91, 16.51 and 15.87. Under the Camarilla method, resistance levels stood at 17.57, 17.73 and 17.88, while support levels were 17.27, 17.11 and 16.96.
 Nifty Gains 1.23% at Opening Before Afternoon Profit-Booking 
 Indian benchmark indices opened sharply higher on Wednesday following the Diwali holiday. At approximately 9:23 AM, the Sensex advanced 1,167.85 points or 1.44% to 82,274.50, while the Nifty 50 gained 307.95 points or 1.23% to 25,352.60. By 11 AM, the Sensex was up 1.55%, while the Nifty had advanced 1.33%.
 However, the benchmarks surrendered a portion of their early gains as the session progressed. At approximately 2 PM, the Sensex was trading 521.52 points or 0.64% higher at 81,628.17, while the Nifty 50 stood at 25,172.05, up 127.40 points or 0.51%. The moderation in gains followed the strong morning advance and reflected profit-booking during the afternoon.
 Sectoral performance remained mixed. The Nifty Bank, Nifty PSU Bank and Nifty Private Bank indices were among the strongest gainers, whereas the Nifty Pharma, Nifty Realty and Nifty IT indices featured among the leading losers. InterGlobe Aviation, Mahindra & Mahindra and State Bank of India were among the leading Nifty 50 gainers in the afternoon update. The Nifty MidCap index advanced 0.68%, while the SmallCap index gained 1.32%.
 Rupee Strengthens 21 Paise as Foreign Equity Inflows Support Currency 
 The Indian rupee opened stronger against the US dollar on 11 November, trading at ₹93.72 per dollar, compared with its previous close of ₹93.93. This represented an initial appreciation of 21 paise. It subsequently strengthened approximately 0.2% to ₹93.75 per dollar.
 Foreign investment inflows supported the currency, although dollar demand from importers limited its gains. Foreign portfolio investors had purchased approximately $5.68 billion worth of Indian equities during November, marking their strongest monthly buying activity since September 2024. This figure represented cumulative November activity and was not the confirmed net purchase amount for 11 November alone.
 US Inflation and Treasury Yields Keep Federal Reserve Policy in Focus 
 Developments surrounding US inflation remained an important global factor during Wednesday’s Indian trading session. The US October Consumer Price Index data showed headline inflation increasing 0.4% month-on-month, while core inflation rose 0.3%, exceeding market expectations of 0.2%.
 The inflation reading strengthened expectations that the US Federal Reserve could maintain tighter monetary conditions for longer. Market expectations of a December rate hike also increased following the data. The US two-year Treasury yield rose approximately 17–18 basis points to 4.73%, while the 10-year Treasury yield stood at approximately 4.99%. The Dollar Index was reported at around 102.28.
 These developments followed the previous US trading session and continued to influence global financial-market conditions during India’s 11 November session. Higher Treasury yields and uncertainty surrounding the Federal Reserve’s monetary-policy direction remained relevant to emerging-market currencies, equity valuations and international capital flows.
 US-Iran Tensions and Crude Oil Movements Keep Energy Risks Relevant 
 Crude oil prices and geopolitical developments involving the US and Iran remained significant components of the global market backdrop. Brent crude traded at approximately $91.85 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) stood near $86.68 in the early morning update. The easing in crude prices followed developments surrounding the US-Iran conflict.
 However, reports of attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and US strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island kept regional energy infrastructure and supply security in focus. Continuing diplomatic uncertainty between Washington and Tehran also remained part of the geopolitical backdrop.
 For India, crude oil prices are relevant to the import bill, inflation, currency movements and operating costs across fuel-dependent industries. Lower international oil prices provided relief during the session, although geopolitical developments continued to feature in global market updates.
 Dow Falls 0.30% as Nasdaq Declines 0.74% Ahead of Indian Trade 
 US equity markets ended the previous trading session lower, providing another external development relevant to Indian markets on Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.30%, the S&P 500 fell 0.38%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.74%.
 The Nasdaq recorded the steepest decline among the three indices amid weakness in technology stocks, including Nvidia. The movements coincided with higher US Treasury yields following the inflation report.
 Asian markets, meanwhile, recorded gains in early trading on 11 November. Japan’s Nikkei advanced 0.73%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 0.44%, and the Shanghai Composite rose 0.08%. South Korean and Australian market updates were mixed.
 Precious metals also recorded movements during the session. COMEX gold recovered towards $4,050 per ounce, while COMEX silver gained more than 2% in the reported morning update. The recovery followed a sharp sell-off on Tuesday after US inflation data strengthened expectations of a possible Federal Reserve rate hike.
 Corporate Results and Policy Announcements Add to Domestic Market Developments 
 Several company-specific announcements and financial results were reported on Wednesday. Kalyan Jewellers recorded a 63.9% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹427.1 crore for the second quarter of FY27, while revenue increased 31.4% to ₹10,322.6 crore. Its shares gained approximately 12.3%, reaching a 52-week high following the earnings announcement.
 Cochin Shipyard reported a 50% decline in consolidated net profit to ₹53.8 crore, despite an 11.7% increase in revenue. Whirlpool of India’s consolidated net profit declined 40% to ₹25.1 crore, while revenue increased 13.7%.
 IIFL Finance announced a preferential capital raise of ₹6,414 crore, including a proposed ₹5,000 crore investment from Blackstone. Ashoka Buildcon received a Letter of Acceptance from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for an expressway project worth ₹865.9 crore. Meanwhile, BHEL received relief after the Telangana Commercial Tax Department dropped a tax demand of ₹207.26 crore.
 The Department of Pharmaceuticals also invited fresh applications under the revamped Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for medical devices. The scheme has an outlay of approximately ₹2,700 crore and covers medical consumables, critical components and high-end medical devices. Its continuation period extends through FY2035-36, with the objective of strengthening domestic manufacturing and reducing import dependence.
 November Records Negative India VIX Returns In 10 Of 18 Years 
 India VIX’s historical seasonality data showed that the index had recorded negative returns in 10 out of 18 years during November. Its average November change stood at 1.20%. The maximum positive change was 21.46% in 2021, while the average positive change was 12.47%. The maximum negative change was 19.92% in 2020, with an average negative change of 7.82%.
 India VIX closed at 17.55, up 0.75%, after trading between 15.64 and 17.82 on 11 November 2026. Domestic benchmark movements, currency developments, corporate announcements and global economic and geopolitical updates formed the key developments of the session. Its daily technical rating remained Neutral, with the pivot point at 17.54.
